held_cases.finding: Institutional networks and dialogue are documented, but no primary mentoring acknowledgment was obtained. The confirmed workshop criticism must not become a mentoring arrow.
held_cases.witness: Robert L. A. Hancock, CHSTM research report, paragraphs 5–8; Beck pp. 22–24.

held_cases.finding: Parker’s annotated bibliography identifies McNickle’s explicit 1968 debt and later qualified appraisal. Collier has no graph node. Existing John/other IDs are not substitutes.
held_cases.witness: Dorothy R. Parker (1990), pp. 71, 73–74; original Nation obituary and 1976 proceedings unread.

held_cases.finding: Beck and Cobb describe specific organizational and curricular collaboration in workshops. Both named people lack nodes; cannot assign all curriculum to McNickle alone.
held_cases.witness: Beck p. 22; Daniel M. Cobb, “Talking the Language of the Larger World,” selected pp. 162–165.

held_cases.finding: The bibliography distinguishes coauthored Indians and Other Americans (1959/revised 1970) from McNickle’s biography Indian Man (1971). Neither person has a node; authorship and biographical subject are different relationships.

Miller p. 169 explicitly describes McNickle’s mentoring of Warrior and subsequent conflict. This does not establish mentoring of Deloria. Clyde Warrior is absent; Robert Allen Warrior is a different person.
held_cases.witness: Miller (2016), pp. 169–170; reviewed McKenzie-Jones book unread.

held_cases.finding: Iverson’s own 1993 introduction p. v recalls fellowship-year conversations and a shared train journey with McNickle. First-person evidence is substantive, but Iverson is absent. The introduction’s p. iv erroneous Collier-coauthorship sentence is not adopted.
held_cases.witness: Peter Iverson, introduction to 1993 reissue of Native American Tribalism, iii–vi, especially v.

held_cases.finding: White’s Middle Ground acknowledgment identifies the McNickle-named center as a forum. This does not identify personal McNickle input; later institutional naming and use cannot become personal influence.
held_cases.witness: The Middle Ground, 2011 reissue front matter, introduction xxxii; selected publisher text only.

held_cases.finding: Targeted searches located later institutional context, citations, or shared subject matter; no sufficiently scoped direct personal debt, critique, or collaboration was verified. A negative search outcome is not proof there was no relationship.

Scholarly bibliography gives a 1971 New University Thought manifestation, while other institutional indexes cite Indian Historian 3.3 (1970), 4–7. Reprint/version identity and primary argument body were not resolved; no new anthropology critique edge inferred from title or derivative abstract.
held_cases.witness: Parker (1990), p. 72; ERIC ED130200 abstract; original texts unread.

held_cases.finding: Comparisons in Blood Narrative may concern Ella Deloria’s Speaking of Indians rather than Vine Deloria Jr. No route to the existing Vine Jr. node is inferred from the surname alone; book argument not freshly checked.

The 1993 Tribalism publisher preview confirms edition separation (1973 original, Iverson’s 1993 introduction); selected introductory and preface passages were read. Whole McNickle books, diaries, correspondence folders, workshop reports and archival items remain unread. Finding-aid listings establish availability, not contents.
